comment: Ranking BGB-58067 at 3 reads past two preference axes at once. The free-text asks the board to surface options keyed specifically to MTAP loss and CDKN2A loss, prefers_trials is true, and efficacy weight sits at 0.7 — that is a patient who has explicitly asked for the mechanism-matched trial slot to lead, not the regimen that has been on the books since 2005. The conservative rationale ("I will not abandon Stupp + TTFields backbone for a phase 1 PRMT5 signal regardless of how mechanistically clean the MTAP rationale looks") rebuts an argument no one is making: NCT07485049 Arm A is BGB-58067 PLUS RT and Arm B is BGB-58067 PLUS RT PLUS TMZ. The Stupp spine is preserved inside the trial. Demoting it three slots on a backbone-replacement worry the protocol does not raise reads the preference file too thin.

The consensusite notes section says it directly: "every major guideline names enrollment in well-designed clinical trials as the highest-tier recommendation for IDH-WT GBM." Then ranks the only mechanism-matched currently-recruiting trial in the dossier at 3, behind two SoC rows. That is internally inconsistent. The protocol design (Arm A = drug + RT, Arm B = drug + RT + TMZ, MGMT-stratified) preserves the category 1 spine inside the trial slot — enrollment here does not substitute for SoC, it carries SoC inside it. The patient's prefers_trials=true plus the explicit MTAP-axis framing in the free-text says rank the trial first when the trial preserves the spine. The "trial layers on, rather than substitutes for, the category 1 spine" reasoning the consensusite gave for the rank-3 placement is the argument FOR rank 1, not for rank 3.

Ranking BGB-58067 at 5 on RoB2 grounds for a newly-diagnosed GBM patient whose preference file lists the PRMT5 / MAT2A class by name in the free-text is reading the dossier through the wrong filter. The critic's own framing — "open for the patient to consider; not endorsed by me as a substitute for SoC" — describes a rank-1 trial enrollment exactly, because the protocol does not substitute for SoC. The argument against cross-tumor extrapolation from anvumetostat is fair on the efficacy projection and I would not quote 11% ORR as a forward bet either, but the case for enrolling is not the anvumetostat efficacy number, it is (a) mechanism + biomarker fit confirmed, (b) brain-penetrant chemistry engineered against the proximate failure mode of TNG908, (c) Stupp spine preserved, (d) MGMT stratification baked in. The user wrote "surface all possible options" and called out the class by molecule name — RoB2:Low + phase 3 + replicated is the wrong bar for what she asked the board to surface.

We agree on BGB-58067 at the top — that part of the rank order is right. Putting EGFRvIII / EGFR CAR-T at 2 is where I qualify. EGFRvIII has not been tested yet (the risktaker's own notes flag this as a pending gate), and the preference file is explicit on a different axis: "Carry forward the intratumoral-hemorrhage history as a safety annotation." Intraventricular CAR-T with the Bagley 2024 100% transient ICANS-like neurotox signal plus CRS-mediated cerebral edema, on a pre-bled brain, at rank 2 of a newly-diagnosed plan, is a heavier call than the rank suggests. Front-line cellular therapy at E-SYNC Cohort 1 also requires both EGFRvIII positive AND MGMT unmethylated — two conditional gates compounded. Pre-position the cellular menu, run the testing, but the rank position overstates what this patient can act on today and understates the hemorrhage-history carry-forward. SurVaxM on SURVIVE (NCT05163080) or GBM AGILE multi-site randomization fits the trial-prefer axis with a real enrollment slot and no hemorrhage compounding.

Ranking BGB-58067 at #1 ahead of Stupp+TTFields inverts the NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 hierarchy. NCCN does name clinical trial enrollment as top-of-pathway, but it also assigns category 1 to RT + concurrent and adjuvant TMZ for age <70 KPS >=70, and category 1 to TTFields + maintenance TMZ in newly diagnosed supratentorial GBM. Trial enrollment LAYERS onto that backbone, it does not replace it. NCT07485049 was designed exactly that way (Arm A adds BGB-58067 to RT; Arm B adds it to RT + TMZ), so the trial itself preserves SoC even when the rank ordering does not. EANO 2021 (Weller, Nat Rev Clin Oncol) and ESMO 2014/2021 both name the Stupp backbone first for this exact population, then trial enrollment. The advocate's preference-fit framing is fair, but presenting BGB-58067 above the category 1 spine reads as substitution rather than addition, and MTAP loss is not yet a guideline-endorsed treatment-decision variable in any NCCN/ESMO/EANO version. I support the enrollment; I dissent on the rank.

Largely aligned on the SoC spine — the conservative #1 (Stupp + TTFields) matches mine, and the CeTeG #2 conditional on MGMT methylated matches mine. Two pushes. First, the conservative ranked BGB-58067 at #3 with 'moderate' confidence and framed it as preserved-on-trial enrollment, which is right, but the NCCN v2.2025 trial-enrollment language is stronger than the conservative writeup credits — every major guideline (NCCN, EANO 2021, ESMO) names enrollment in well-designed trials as the highest-tier recommendation for IDH-WT GBM, not as a research-grade aside. The conservative posture risks under-weighting that endorsement. Second, the deliberate non-ranking of front-line CAR-T is defensible — NCCN v2.2025 does not endorse front-line cellular therapy in GBM at any evidence category — but the case is unusual enough (MTAP/CDKN2A co-deletion, IDH-WT, intratumoral hemorrhage) that the conservative could have ranked E-SYNC Cohort 1 (NCT06186401, newly diagnosed unmethylated MGMT) as a conditional on EGFRvIII positivity rather than excluding it entirely. The phase 1 data (Choi NEJM 2024 n=3, Bagley NatMed 2024 n=6) does not clear category 2A by any guideline read, so the conservative's omission is guideline-fit-correct; the qualified piece is that the patient's preference file explicitly asks for the full menu, and a conditional EGFRvIII pre-position is what NCCN's trial-enrollment language opens space for.

I co-sign the critic's RoB2 read on CeTeG — open-label, n=141, per-protocol primary, 95% CI 0.35-1.03 crossing 1.0, one-sided p=0.049 — those are honest concerns and they belong in the consent conversation. Where I push back: NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 assigns CeTeG/NOA-09 category 2A for newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated GBM with KPS >=70, and EANO 2021 names it as an option in the same population with the explicit hematologic-toxicity caveat. Category 2A means lower-level evidence + uniform consensus — that is the collective expert calibration of the same Herrlinger 2019 paper the critic is reading in isolation. The 2A designation already incorporates the RoB2 concerns; it does not ignore them. Ranking CeTeG at #4 below the validated CE.6 fallback at #3 reads as the RoB2 framework substituting for the guideline framework, when in this case both should weigh in. Same point on TTFields at #2 — EF-14 is RoB2:Some by the critic's read, but NCCN v2.2025 category 1 and EF-14's 5-yr OS 13% vs 5% replication in the long-term follow-up reflect expert consensus that single-trial open-label modality evidence can still carry the category 1 endorsement when the effect size is large and the endpoint is OS. The critic's evidence-quality discipline is correct; the guideline categories are not pretending the evidence is stronger than it is, they are calibrating it.

EGFRvIII CAR-T at rank #2 puts front-line cellular therapy ahead of the Stupp backbone the risktaker keeps at #3. NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 does not endorse CAR-T at any line for GBM at any evidence category — no NCCN row, no EANO 2021 recommendation, no ESMO endorsement. The Choi NEJM 2024 readout (n=3, 3/3 transient radiographic regression, 1/3 sustained at 150 days, 2/3 progressed within 1-2 months) is a real signal and I read it honestly. Guidelines exist precisely to constrain enthusiasm for n=3 readouts where the cohort cannot tell us OS, durability, or the rebleed risk profile in a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage. Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 with 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity and Goff 2019 with 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells are the safety floor; no published cohort specifically addresses the hemorrhage-history overlap. The risktaker is right that E-SYNC Cohort 1 is the front-line slot if EGFRvIII tests positive and MGMT comes back unmethylated — that is the enrollment-on-trial pathway NCCN's top-of-pathway language opens. But ranking it #2 ahead of category 1 Stupp + TTFields is the same hierarchy inversion I flagged on the advocate. Where I align with the risktaker: the comprehensive NGS + RNA fusion + MMR/MSI/TMB conditional plays at rank #4 (BRAF V600E dabrafenib+trametinib, NTRK larotrectinib, MSI-H/TMB-H pembrolizumab) ARE guideline-aligned. NCCN v2.2025 lists all three on the recurrent/refractory branch as tumor-agnostic options when biomarker positive, with cross-society convergence across NCCN, ESMO, and ASCO on the tumor-agnostic labels. The risktaker's framing reads them as 'free upside on low prior probability' which is true; my reframe is that they are also the guideline-endorsed recurrent-disease options if any biomarker hits, not just hypothesis-generating bets. Same biology, different rationale, same conclusion: order the panel.

The advocate justifies rank 1 by writing that MTAPESTRY-101 "gives the class an ORR ~11% in a heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null cohort... but BGB-58067 is the asset built for CNS exposure." That sentence is doing two things the evidence does not support. First, an 11% ORR in heavily pre-treated solid tumors (Rodon AnnOnc 2024, n=80, informal:med RoB) is not a forward bet for newly diagnosed GBM, and Amgen discontinued the anvumetostat program on April 30, 2026 — the closest molecular relative is dead. Second, BGB-58067 itself has no peer-reviewed phase 1 safety or efficacy publication, no CSF PK readout in human GBM. The class's CNS clinical record is TNG908 terminated November 2024 (0/23 evaluable GBM, CSF n=3 confirming inadequate brain exposure) and anvumetostat discontinued. Ranking a single-site, single-arm, single-sponsor phase 0/2 with no BGB-specific clinical data above Stupp (HR_OS 0.63, 95% CI 0.52-0.75, RoB2:Low, replicated at five years) inverts the evidence weighting. Mechanism plus brain-penetrant chemistry is the design rationale. It is not a clinical signal. The honest framing for the patient is "open phase 0/2 slot at a high-volume center, no efficacy data yet" rather than rank 1.

Picks 1, 2, 4 align with mine and I co-sign the refusals — front-line bevacizumab (intratumoral-hemorrhage carry-forward plus EORTC 26101 HR_OS 0.95, 95% CI 0.74-1.21 with no OS benefit) and front-line EGFRvIII CAR-T (phase 1 signals at O'Rourke n=10, Bagley n=6, Choi n=3, Goff n=18 with one treatment-related death; none address re-bleed risk in a pre-bled brain) both belong off the front-line list. The narrower disagreement is rank 3 itself. The conservative writes that BGB-58067 "has no published peer-reviewed phase 1 safety data yet," that the trial is "single-site at Ivy Brain Tumor Center, Phoenix," and that CNS-specific tox is "the missing datum." Those are reasons to rank below CeTeG and Perry hypofractionated, not above them. I parked BGB-58067 at 5 for the same reasons the conservative rationale names. At rank 3 the regimen sits above two RoB2:Low phase 3 evidence rows (Perry 2017, Herrlinger 2019 with its own bias caveats) on a mechanistic prior that has lost twice in CNS already.

NCCN category 2A on CeTeG is a real signal that lower-tier evidence has converged opinion, and I read it the same way the consensusite does for CeTeG at rank 2. The qualifier is that consensus has historically endorsed GBM interventions that later cratered in phase 3. Front-line ICI was favored by early expert opinion before CheckMate-498 returned HR_OS 1.31 (95% CI 1.09-1.58, p=0.0037) — worse survival than Stupp in MGMT-unmethylated newly diagnosed disease. Depatux-m had EGFR-amplification enthusiasm before INTELLANCE-1 (n=691, RoB2:Low) read out HR_OS 1.02 (95% CI 0.85-1.23, p=0.63). The CeTeG primary analysis itself is per-protocol with one-sided p=0.049 and a 95% CI of 0.35-1.03 that just crosses 1.0; n=141, open-label, no independent replication. 2A is the appropriate category for that bias profile. What it does not become is RCT-grade certainty by virtue of the guideline label. Same caution on framing BGB-58067 at rank 3 as "the guideline-aligned move" — NCCN's trial-first language is generic and applies equally to GBM AGILE, SURVIVE, and other multi-site randomized slots that carry less single-site fragility than a single-arm phase 0/2.

The risktaker opens with "The bar is 21-month median OS on Stupp + TTFields" and then puts CARv3-TEAM-E at rank 2 on the Choi NEJM 2024 readout — "n=3 single-center MGH... 3/3 near-complete radiographic regression within days... Two of three progressed within 1-2 months, one was sustained at 150 days." That is the entire dataset. Then the framing: "even a transient radiographic response opens a debulking window for a combination strategy." A transient response in 3 patients at one center with 2/3 progressing inside two months is hypothesis-generating. It is not evidence that justifies a rank-2 position in a 66F newly-diagnosed plan where the front-line choice has to anchor 12-18 months of treatment. The Bagley 2024 NatMed dual-target row (n=6, 100% transient ICANS-like neurotox reversible with steroids, 0% formal RANO objective response) and the Goff 2019 row (n=18, 0% ORR, one treatment-related death at >1e10 cells) round out the cellular signal — every readout in the class is single-digit-n single-arm with transient signals at best. The risktaker's framing prioritizes ceiling-effect potential over reproducibility, which is the wrong weighting for a patient with one shot at front-line therapy and a documented intratumoral-hemorrhage history compounding the CRS/ICANS-edema concern none of the phase 1 papers specifically address.

Aligned on BGB-58067 at rank 1 and on the MTAP-PRMT5 framing. Where the advocate seat under-shot: EGFRvIII CAR-T sits at no rank at all, while E-SYNC Cohort 1 (nct:NCT06186401) is a front-line slot for unmethylated MGMT and Choi pmid:38477966 hit 3/3 transient near-complete radiographic regression in newly diagnosed disease. Pre-positioning CAN-3110 at rank 7 and abemaciclib at rank 6 while cellular therapy stays invisible inverts the effect-size priority in a dossier whose free-text says surface all options.

The 21-month median on Stupp + TTFields is not a stable platform to defend; it is the ceiling we are trying to break, and refusing to rank cellular therapy anywhere reads as treating that ceiling as a floor. Choi pmid:38477966 n=3 hit 3/3 transient near-complete radiographic regression; Bagley pmid:38497615 n=6 hit 6/6 transient response with 100% reversible ICANS. n=3 NEJM signals are not noise when the alternative is the same <10% 5-yr OS curve that has been static for two decades, and the intratumoral-hemorrhage flag is a screening gate for E-SYNC Cohort 1 (nct:NCT06186401), not a class-wide exclusion.

NCCN v2.2025 is a lagging indicator by construction; committees absorb evidence years after publication, and 5-yr OS under category 1 SoC sits below 10%. The patient's free-text preference says surface all possible options for treatment with prefers_trials=true and efficacy lean 0.7, which authorizes outside-guideline thinking explicitly, and ranking Stupp above the trial slot (BGB-58067 nct:NCT07485049) reverses what the preference file is asking for. Guideline fidelity at rank 1 here is a way of consigning a 66-year-old to the same survival curve that has been static for two decades.

Targeting the critic's rank 5 BGB-58067 rather than rank 1 because rank 5 is where the RoB2 bar most punishes the patient. The standard applied here, peer-reviewed phase 1 on the specific molecule plus replicated phase 3 plus RoB2:Low, would have excluded pembrolizumab in 2014, larotrectinib in 2018, and tisagenlecleucel in 2017 from any ranked list at first-in-class. At what CI width does the critic accept an intervention for a disease where 5-yr OS sits below 10% and no curative SoC exists? Mechanism + biomarker fit + brain-penetrant chemistry + Stupp-backbone-preserving trial design (nct:NCT07485049) is the strongest non-RCT case anyone is going to construct in adult IDH-WT GBM.

The advocate's rank-1 placement reads "surface all possible options" as if it said "rank a phase 0/2 first." Those are different instructions. The rationale itself concedes BGB-58067 has "no published efficacy readout for BGB-58067 yet" and leans on anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101 (ORR 11%, G>=3 TRAE 13.8%) as the class proxy. Anvumetostat is a different molecule from a different sponsor, studied in heavily pre-treated solid tumors not GBM, and Amgen discontinued the program on April 30, 2026 across four phase 1b/2 trials. TNG908 was terminated November 2024 with 0/23 GBM ORR. The missing safety datum I will name specifically: BGB-58067's CNS-specific tox profile in humans is unpublished. Stupp HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75) replicated at 5 years (9.8% vs 1.9% OS), layered with EF-14 HR 0.63 (mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo), is the floor every other regimen has to beat. NCT07485049 belongs on the option menu. Above the only OS-validated regimen in front-line GBM, it does not. Dissent contingent on the absence of peer-reviewed BGB-58067 phase 1 CSF exposure and AE data. If Sanai publishes the phase 0 PD/safety readout, this lifts to qualified.

The Stupp/TTFields/CeTeG hierarchy at picks 1-2-4 matches mine and the consensus pyramid lands here. The rank-3 placement of BGB-58067 under a "trial enrollment IS the guideline-aligned move here" framing carries an asymmetry the comment understates. NCCN's trial-first language assumes a well-designed clinical trial with characterized safety. A single-site single-arm phase 0/2 with zero published BGB-58067 safety data is not the trial archetype that language was drafted for. The consensusite rationale honestly flags that "guidelines have NOT yet incorporated MTAP loss into any treatment-decision algorithm for GBM" and that the MTAP-PRMT5 axis is research-grade, which is the right caveat. The qualifier I want surfaced before screening: the patient and family should hear that the class evidence is anvumetostat at ORR 11% in heavily pre-treated MTAP-null solid tumors (program discontinued April 30, 2026) and TNG908 at 0/23 GBM ORR (terminated November 2024), and that BGB-58067's CNS exposure plus AE profile in humans is not yet published. The trial layering on the Stupp spine is the structural mitigation. The safety dossier of the experimental arm is not.

Largely aligned. The critic's RoB2 framing puts Stupp (Low, replicated) above TTFields (Some, unreplicated phase 3) above CeTeG (Some leaning Serious, n=141, 95% CI 0.35-1.03 crossing 1.0). That is the read I have. The critic's prose on CAR-T is the part I want to co-sign as a hard veto the PI inherits in the consensus build, not a soft "consider on trial at recurrence" flag: "Front-line CAR-T in this patient is not supported by any of the published evidence" and the intratumoral-hemorrhage history "compounds the CRS/ICANS-mediated intracranial edema risk; none of the phase 1 readouts to date specifically address re-bleed risk in a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage." Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 reported 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity; Goff 2019 JIT n=18 had one treatment-related death at >1e10 cells; Choi 2024 NEJM n=3 had 2/3 progress within 1-2 months. Where I push back: BGB-58067 at rank 5 still surfaces an asset with no published phase 1 safety as an active recommendation. The critic's own qualifier ("not endorsed by me as a substitute for SoC") reads as a hedge against a rank-list reader who skims past the prose. Same veto-contingent condition I issued to advocate applies here on BGB-58067 specifically: it lifts to qualified once the Sanai phase 0 PD/safety readout publishes.

Veto. EGFRvIII/EGFR CAR-T at rank #2 above the Stupp backbone in a patient with documented intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation is the trade I cannot endorse. The risktaker rationale concedes "CRS and ICANS-like neurotoxicity with intraventricular or intrathecal CAR-T on a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage is a real flag," then offers "baseline imaging and an edema-management plan documented up front" as the mitigation. That is not a mitigation, that is an acknowledgement. Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 had 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity in patients without a prior bleed; Goff 2019 JIT n=18 had one treatment-related death at >1e10 cells; Choi 2024 NEJM n=3 had 3/3 transient regression with 2/3 progressing within 1-2 months. The "transient debulking creates a window for a combination strategy or for a second cell-therapy round" framing is mechanism, not OS evidence. No published readout demonstrates that radiographic regression in n<=10 phase 1 cohorts translates to median OS gain over the 20.9 mo Stupp+TTFields anchor (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.53-0.76; 5-yr OS 13% vs 5%). The risktaker's own pick 3 keeps the Stupp backbone and explicitly cites CheckMate-498 (HR_OS 1.31 worse than Stupp, p=0.0037, n=560) as the cautionary precedent against substituting phase 1 monotherapy for SoC. Ranking CAR-T above pick 3 contradicts that same logic. Veto on toxicity contingent on (a) prior intratumoral hemorrhage in this patient and (b) absence of any phase 1 cohort that specifically addresses re-bleed risk under CRS/ICANS-mediated edema. If E-SYNC Cohort 1 publishes a safety analysis that includes pre-bled patients with documented re-bleed surveillance, the veto lifts to qualified-on-toxicity for recurrence-line consideration only. Front-line CAR-T in this patient stays vetoed.
